verses.text: Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would live in thick darkness.
But I have built a wonderful temple for you, a place for you to live forever."
Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel while they all stood there.
He said, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel! With his own mouth he made a promise to my father David, and with his own hands he has kept it. He said,

'Since the day I brought my people out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel to build a temple for my name to be there. And I have not chosen anyone to be the leader of my people Israel.
But now I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to rule my people Israel.'
My father David wanted with all his heart to build a temple to honour the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, 'You wanted with all your heart to build a temple for my name. It was good that you wanted to do this.
But you will not build the temple. Your own son will build the temple for my name.'

Now the LORD has kept the promise he made. I have taken my father David's place, and I sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised. And I have built the temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
I have put the ark there. In it is the LORD's covenant that he made with the people of Israel."
Then Solomon stood before the LORD's altar in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

Solomon had made a bronze platform about two metres long, two metres wide, and over a metre high, and had put it in the middle of the courtyard. He stood on it, then knelt down in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven.
He prayed, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth. You keep your covenant and show faithful love to your servants who follow you with all their hearts.
You have kept your promise to your servant David, my father. With your mouth you promised, and with your hand you have done it, as we see today.

Now, LORD, God of Israel, keep the other promise you made to your servant David, my father. You said, 'You will always have a descendant to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your children are careful to live by my law as you have done.'
Now, LORD, God of Israel, let the promise you made to your servant David come true.
But will God really live on earth with people? Even the heavens, the highest heavens, cannot hold you. How much less this temple I have built!
Yet please listen to your servant's prayer and his request, LORD my God. Hear the cry and the prayer your servant is praying to you.
Watch over this temple day and night. This is the place where you said you would put your name. Hear the prayer your servant prays toward this place.
Listen to the requests of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, where you live, and when you hear, forgive.
If someone wrongs their neighbour and is made to swear an oath, and comes and swears before your altar in this temple,
then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants. Punish the guilty one as they deserve, and declare the innocent one innocent, rewarding them for doing right.
If your people Israel are beaten by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and then they turn back to you, praise your name, and pray and beg before you in this temple,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel. Bring them back to the land you gave to them and their ancestors.
When the sky is shut and there is no rain because your people have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place, praise your name, and turn from their sin because you have punished them,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on your land, the land you gave your people as their own.
If there is hunger in the land, or disease, or crops ruined by hot winds or mould, or locusts or grasshoppers; or if enemies surround any of their cities; whatever disaster or sickness comes,
and someone, or all your people Israel, prays and begs you for help, each one knowing their own trouble and pain, and spreads out their hands toward this temple,
then hear from heaven, where you live, and forgive. Give each person what they deserve for everything they do, since you know their hearts. Only you know what is in people's hearts.
Then they will respect you and follow your ways for as long as they live in the land you gave our ancestors.
Also, a foreigner who is not one of your people Israel may come from a far country because of your great name, your mighty hand, and your powerful arm. When they come and pray toward this temple,

then hear from heaven, where you live, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you. Then all the peoples of the earth will know your name and respect you, as your people Israel do. They will know that this temple I have built carries your name.
When your people go out to fight their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to you toward this city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name,
then hear their prayer and their request from heaven, and help them win.
When they sin against you, for there is no one who does not sin, and you are angry with them and hand them over to their enemies, who take them away as prisoners to a land far away or near,
then if they change their hearts in the land where they are prisoners, and turn back and beg you there, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'

and if they return to you with all their heart and soul in the land where they were taken, and pray toward the land you gave their ancestors, toward the city you have chosen, and toward the temple I have built for your name,
then hear their prayer and requests from heaven, where you live. Help them, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
Now, my God, please let your eyes be open and your ears listen to the prayers made in this place.
Now rise up, LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your power. LORD God, let your priests be clothed with salvation, and let your faithful people rejoice in your goodness.
LORD God, do not turn away from your anointed king. Remember your faithful love for your servant David."
